files.content:
/**
 * The field anatomy, shared by every control that wears it — `TextField`,
 * `SearchField`, and the textarea, select, checkbox and radio still to come.
 *
 * Only the styling lives here. Each component defines its own slot components,
 * thin as they are, so that its docs and manifest describe its own API rather
 * than pointing at another component's.
 */

/**
 * The three control sizes. `size` is set once on the field and travels as two
 * custom properties rather than through React context: the control, and any
 * affix inside it, are ordinary descendants of the field, so inheritance already
 * does the work. It also means a one-off override is just a utility on the
 * element rather than a new prop.
 */
export type FieldSize = 'sm' | 'md' | 'lg'

export const FIELD_SIZES: Record<FieldSize, string> = {
  sm: '[--field-control-h:2.25rem] [--field-control-text:0.8125rem]', // 36px / 13px
  md: '[--field-control-h:2.75rem] [--field-control-text:0.875rem]', // 44px / 14px
  lg: '[--field-control-h:3.25rem] [--field-control-text:0.9375rem]', // 52px / 15px
}

/**
 * The sheet's `.ds-field`: legend, control, then the hint that explains it.
 *
 * The `font-size` here is what the control and any affix inherit. It sits on the
 * field rather than on the input so it still reaches an affix, which is the
 * input's sibling — a `cap`-sized icon would otherwise match the page's font
 * instead of the field's.
 *
 * The two border properties are published here for the same reason `Checkbox`
 * publishes its own: read-only lives on the field root, while the border it changes
 * is on the input, and a group variant cannot win that cascade — see the note on
 * `INPUT`. Declaring them here means the input only reads them, and the ordinary
 * cascade decides, because `[data-readonly]` plainly outranks the bare declaration.
 */
export const FIELD = [
  'group flex flex-col gap-2 [font-size:var(--field-control-text)]',
  '[--field-border:var(--color-line-control)]',
  '[--field-hover:var(--color-line)]',
  // Read-only is not disabled: the value is the whole point of the field, so it
  // keeps full-strength text. Only the affordances go — a quieter hairline, and no
  // brightening on hover — because there is nothing here to invite a click on.
  'data-[readonly]:[--field-border:var(--color-line-soft)]',
  'data-[readonly]:[--field-hover:var(--color-line-soft)]',
].join(' ')

/**
 * The sheet's `.ds-affix` wrapper. `Group` exists for one case: an affix is
 * positioned against the control, but the field also holds the legend and the
 * hint, so an affix anchored to the field would centre on all three.
 * Wrapping the control gives the affix the right box — and it stays opt-in, so a
 * plain field has no extra element at all.
 *
 * The two `:has()` rules are here for the same reason: the room an affix needs is
 * padding on the input, and the group is what can see both of them. The input
 * itself never has to know it has neighbours.
 */
export const GROUP = [
  'relative flex w-full',
  'has-[[data-slot=icon-start]]:[&>[data-slot=input]]:ps-10.5', // 42px, per the sheet's search field
  'has-[[data-slot=icon-end]]:[&>[data-slot=input]]:pe-14', // 56px, per the sheet's trailing unit
].join(' ')

/**
 * The sheet's `.ds-field-legend`: 12px, uppercase, letterspaced, white 70%.
 *
 * The required marker is drawn from the field's own `data-required`, so the label
 * never has to be told and the asterisk cannot drift out of sync with
 * `isRequired`. The input already carries the native `required`, so this is the
 * visual half of the same fact.
 */
export const LABEL = [
  'text-[12px] uppercase tracking-[0.04em] text-fg-muted',
  "group-data-[required]:after:ms-1 group-data-[required]:after:text-red group-data-[required]:after:content-['*']",
].join(' ')

/**
 * The sheet's `.ds-input`.
 *
 * The resting hairline is what identifies the control. The sheet gives
 * `.ds-input` a transparent border and leaves the panel-2 fill to do the job, but
 * that fill is 1.23:1 on the dark page and 1.17:1 on the light one, so the field is
 * nearly invisible as a boundary in both. `--color-line-control` is the smallest
 * hairline that clears the 3:1 a control boundary needs on each.
 *
 * Hover has to *strengthen* it rather than replace it: the sheet's hover is white
 * at 25%, which is now weaker than the resting line and would erase it.
 *
 * `outline-none` on focus suppresses the *browser's* ring, which is what the
 * sheet's `.ds-input:focus { outline: none }` is really doing. Chrome gives a
 * focused text input its `:focus-visible` ring at `outline-style: auto` regardless
 * of React Aria's attribute, so leaving it alone means a blue UA ring on a teal
 * system. Focus is then the border alone — adding the shared 3px-offset ring here
 * would draw two parallel teal hairlines with a gap, which reads as a fault.
 * `Button` can carry that ring because the edge it repeats is a solid fill.
 */
export const INPUT = [
  'w-full font-mono rounded-none border border-(--field-border)',
  'h-(--field-control-h) px-3.5',
  'bg-panel-2 text-fg placeholder:text-fg/35',
  'transition-[border-color,background-color] duration-[120ms] ease-pulse',
  // Focus and invalid stay literal, so they outrank the published border and always
  // win — including on a read-only field, which is still focusable and still the
  // field the caret should be able to reach.
  'data-[hovered]:not-data-[focused]:border-(--field-hover)',
  'data-[focused]:outline-none data-[focused]:border-teal',
  'data-[invalid]:not-data-[focused]:border-red',
  'data-[disabled]:cursor-not-allowed data-[disabled]:opacity-40',
  // Read-only gets the cursor and nothing else that dims it. `opacity` here would
  // take the *value* down with it — at 40% the text measures 3.42:1, under the 4.5:1
  // body text needs, so the one thing the user came to read becomes the thing they
  // cannot.
  'group-data-[readonly]:cursor-not-allowed',
].join(' ')

/** The sheet's `.ds-hint`: 12px, tighter tracking, white 55%. */
export const HINT = 'text-[12px] tracking-[-0.5px] text-fg/55'

/**
 * The sheet paints its error state yellow, because the original design had only
 * two accents and yellow was the nearest thing to a warning it owned. That does
 * not carry over here: `--color-yellow` is this system's `secondary` button, so
 * errors would be the same colour as a secondary action. The error state uses
 * `--color-red`, the danger hue, and keeps the sheet's flex so an icon can be
 * dropped in front of the message.
 */
export const ERROR =
  'flex items-center gap-1.5 text-[12px] tracking-[-0.5px] text-red'

/**
 * The sheet's `.ds-affix__unit` and `.ds-affix__icon`: pinned to the control's
 * box, vertically centred, and never a click target — the affix is decoration, and
 * a pointer-events-owning overlay would swallow clicks meant for the field. Sized
 * in `cap` like `Button.Icon`, so one icon works at every field `size`.
 */
export const ICON = [
  'absolute inset-y-0 z-10 grid place-items-center pointer-events-none',
  'text-fg/70',
  '[&>svg]:block [&>svg]:h-[1.5cap] [&>svg]:w-auto [&>svg]:shrink-0',
].join(' ')

/** The sheet insets both affixes 14px from their edge. */
export const ICON_POSITIONS = {
  start: 'start-3.5',
  end: 'end-3.5',
} as const

export type IconPosition = keyof typeof ICON_POSITIONS

docs:
Two controls, one anatomy. Each is a control, and each carries the group it belongs to as
a slot — so the compound form covers the whole control, not just its decorations:

```tsx
<Radio.Group defaultValue="https">
  <Radio.Label>Protocol</Radio.Label>
  <Radio value="http">
    <Radio.Indicator />
    <Radio.Text>HTTP</Radio.Text>
  </Radio>
  <Radio.Hint>Applies to every check.</Radio.Hint>
  <Radio.Error>Choose a protocol.</Radio.Error>
</Radio.Group>
```

`Checkbox` mirrors it exactly, with `Checkbox.Group`, `.Indicator`, `.Text`, `.Label`,
`.Hint` and `.FieldError`. The slots are explicit, like `Button.Icon` and `Button.Text`; a
bare text child still renders, it just misses the label styling, so a missing slot degrades
rather than disappears.

| Slot                 | React Aria                     | Notes                                                         |
| -------------------- | ------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `Radio` / `Checkbox` | `Radio` / `Checkbox`           | The control. Owns the selection when outside a group          |
| `.Group`             | `RadioGroup` / `CheckboxGroup` | Owns it when inside one; `value` identifies the control to it |
| `.Indicator`         | —                              | The dot or the box, drawn for you                             |
| `.Text`              | —                              | One control's label                                           |
| `.Label`             | `Label`                        | The group's legend — the same `.ds-field-legend` as a field   |
| `.Hint`              | `Text`                         | `slot="description"`, so it is described-by                   |
| `.FieldError`        | `FieldError`                   | Renders nothing while the group is valid                      |

`isRequired` and `isInvalid` live on the **group**, not the control: a `Radio` outside one
has no group state to read. React Aria splits validity two ways — the group gets
`data-invalid` as a styling hook, while `aria-invalid` goes on each control, because the
group is not a focusable thing a screen reader could land on.

### State travels as custom properties, not group variants

The control root is where React Aria puts `data-selected`, `data-hovered` and the rest, so a
rule reaching the indicator has to go through a group variant — and **group variants sort at
the same specificity as a plain utility**, because Tailwind wraps the ancestor in `:where()`.
`group-data-[hovered]:border-fg` therefore ties with the indicator's own
`border-line-control` and loses on source order, silently.

Instead the root publishes `--selection-border`, `--selection-bg`, `--selection-mark`,
`--selection-scale` and `--selection-ring`, and the indicator only reads them. Both rules
then land on the same element, where `[data-selected][data-hovered]` plainly outranks
`[data-hovered]` and the ordinary cascade decides. `Checkbox` and `Radio` publish the same
names deliberately, so neither has to know which it is.

The ring is a transparent outline at rest rather than `outline-none`, so it fades in with
everything else instead of switching the outline on and off.

### Indeterminate is a third state, drawn as a dash

`isIndeterminate` fills the box exactly as a checked one does and shows a **dash** instead of a
tick — the difference between "all of it" and "some of it". React Aria renders `data-indeterminate`
for it, and the tick and the dash sit in the box's single grid cell, so swapping one for the other
cannot change the box's size.

The tick's rule has to **exclude** the indeterminate one. An indeterminate checkbox is usually a
selected one too, so `data-[selected]:[--selection-mark:1]` and `data-[indeterminate]:[…]` would tie
on specificity and source order would decide whether a "some" checkbox showed a tick. Written as
`data-[selected]:not-data-[indeterminate]:` only one of them ever matches.

### The state is a property, not an attribute

A native checkbox reports "mixed" through the **`indeterminate` DOM property**, and nothing writes
it into the markup — so `aria-checked` is absent from it, and `toHaveAttribute('aria-checked',
'mixed')` fails with `null`. Assert `input.indeterminate` and `input.checked`. The browser is what
tells assistive tech it is mixed.

### Three things that make these tests lie

- **The indicator transitions, the input does not.** Reading a colour or an opacity straight
  after a state change returns the old value mid-transition. Freeze `[data-slot=indicator]` or
  `[data-slot=centre]`, not the input.
- **Tailwind v4's `scale-*` sets the standalone `scale` property, not `transform`**, so
  `getComputedStyle(el).transform` stays `'none'` however scaled.
- **`rounded-full` is `border-radius: calc(infinity * 1px)`**, which Chrome computes to
  `3.35544e+07px`. "Is it a circle" has to be asked as "is the radius at least half the box",
  not compared against `'50%'`.
